solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Approve pub bar's term for concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up from ingredients, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker asks a landlord what the bar calls its house cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' sounds like a drink on the bar menu, but it signals the rearrangement of PUBBARSTERM.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp a proposal is to give it automatic official approval, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Aggressive male behaviour Proust regularly exhibited

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, at evenly spaced intervals

explanation.surface: Remarks that the French novelist showed macho aggression from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: The rut is the mating season of male deer, when stags fight and bellow.

clue.text: Havana needs this vehicle reversing on city's outskirts

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A taxi backs up on the edge of the Cuban capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Havana' is the city in the surface, but in the definition it is a cigar, which needs tobacco. BACCY is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A Havana cigar is rolled from tobacco, so the slang word names what it is made of.

clue.text: Eastern male, messenger casting the first stone

indicators.note: casting off the first letter drops the initial of the word

parts.note: a herald is a messenger

explanation.surface: Echoes 'let him cast the first stone', said of an Eastern man.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical 'cast the first stone' is borrowed: 'casting the first' drops H from HERALD, and 'stone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, a gem.

clue.text: Minor cleric's case bound to collapse

indicators.note: letters that collapse fall in a heap and are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A junior churchman is a basket case bound to fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric ranking below a deacon, one of the minor orders.

clue.text: View that could be right

definitions.meaning: a point of view or slant on a story
a right ... is one sort, at ninety degrees

explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as 'correct' but refers to a right angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a perspective on something, and also the space between two lines, which may be a right one.

clue.text: Farmland beyond river

parts.note: past means beyond, as in just past the gate
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Fields lie on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grazing land, a kind of farmland covered with grass.

clue.text: Patient man's situation?

definitions.meaning: ... of the Old Testament is the proverbial model of patience under suffering
a situation is a post or position of employment

explanation.walkthrough: The 'patience of Job' is a stock phrase, which is why he is simply 'Patient man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the biblical figure famed for patience, and a post someone holds at work.

clue.text: Emperor newly arrived in housing area

parts.note: something just in has only now arrived

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one word contains the other

explanation.surface: A ruler has recently moved into a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In housing area' looks like a place, but 'housing' puts A inside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Justinian I was the sixth-century Byzantine ruler famed for codifying Roman law.

clue.text: Little urban ground for high-speed transport

indicators.note: ground as in crushed, broken up and reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: A small patch of city land is set aside for a fast railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as a plot of land; it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet train is a very fast passenger train, like the Japanese Shinkansen.

clue.text: Person pushing in to seize Victorian lunchbox

parts.note: one who tucks in, eating heartily or pushing something in, is a tucker
to bag something is to grab or capture it

explanation.surface: A queue-jumper grabs a lunchbox in nineteenth-century England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the era of Queen Victoria, but it means from Victoria, the Australian state; a tuckerbag is Australian slang for a bag carrying food ('tucker').
explanation.definitionFit: Australian bush slang for the bag in which a traveller carries provisions, a lunchbox of sorts.

clue.text: Maiden crossing island brought back hemp, of a sort

indicators.note: brought back means the combined letters are read in the reverse direction
the girl's letters stretch across, and so enclose, the letter for the island

parts.note: a maiden is a lass, a young unmarried woman
I is the standard abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A young woman sails across to an island and returns with some hemp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' puts I inside LASS to make LAISS; 'brought back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre used for rope and twine, loosely classed among the hemps.

clue.text: What it's said 007 has on invasive code?

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is to be heard, matching another spelling in sound

parts.note: 007 is James Bond, a spy, and what he has on is his clothing, his wear

explanation.surface: Asks what malicious software James Bond has been infected with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has on' reads as 'is infected with' but means 'is wearing', giving 'spy wear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spyware is malicious software that installs itself secretly to watch what a user does.

clue.text: Single fleas in contortions forming their own bond

indicators.note: contortions twist things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone flea is twisting itself about.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-sealing envelopes and tyres close or seal without extra glue, making their own bond.

clue.text: Dodgy individual giving ninety the sack

indicators.note: giving someone the sack means dismissing them, so the letters for the number are dropped

parts.note: something individual, belonging to one only, is exclusive
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shady character fires ninety staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' tempts as a noun's adjective for the individual, but it is the definition in its sense of evasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dodgy in the sense of hard to pin down or evasive is slippery and hard to catch.

clue.text: Made great strides and took charge of fencing work

indicators.note: a fence surrounds something, so the leader's letters enclose the work's

parts.note: to lead is to take charge of, past tense led
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone made big progress and ran the fencing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing work' reads as a trade, but 'fencing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long bounding strides, so the past tense matches making great strides.

clue.text: Dad participating wholeheartedly, to one's embarrassment

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
in, as in 'count me in', means taking part
fully means completely, wholeheartedly

explanation.surface: A father joining in with gusto embarrasses his children.
explanation.definitionFit: Painfully, as in painfully shy, means so as to cause distress or awkwardness.

clue.text: Nurse with extra energy, first person determined to get on

indicators.note: the energy letter is an extra one slipped into the nurse's letters

parts.note: a carer nurses and looks after someone
E is the physics symbol for energy
first written as 1ST, with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A nurse with fresh energy is the first to be ambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' looks like the pronoun I, but 'first' as 1ST gives IST. The definition is adjectival: a careerist can be a careerist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A careerist is chiefly concerned with advancing their own career, ambitious to get ahead.

clue.text: During reports, Officer in Command is moved

indicators.note: during means within a span, so the officer's letters go inside the reports

parts.note: relates means reports or recounts
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: Reports say the commanding officer has been posted elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relocates moves home or base to a new place.

clue.text: Plain cash released for Panama, perhaps

indicators.note: letters set free from their order may fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Simple money was freed up to fund something in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama, perhaps' could suggest a hat; it is the canal, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal is a famous example of a waterway built for ocean-going vessels.

clue.text: With nothing on Persian maybe grabs some entertainment

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it inside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a Persian is a breed of cat
bare means naked, with nothing on

explanation.surface: A naked Persian man catches a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' suggests a person; it is the long-haired cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment with song, dance or comedy at a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Here's something to drink, after knocking back dram — cheers

indicators.note: knocking back a drink sounds like downing it, but here the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a dram is a nip, a small measure of spirits
TA is British informal thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a whisky, says thanks and is handed another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' is drinking talk but signals reversal. A PINTA is British slang for a pint of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pint, usually of milk, from the advertising slogan 'Drinka pinta milka day'.

clue.text: Please old ambassador in ceremony, quietly taking the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means the quiet letter goes in front

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: the ambassador sits in the ceremony, so his letters go inside

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A former ambassador quietly leads a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: the answer is an archaic word for please.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic contraction of 'I pray thee', used as a polite request in old texts.

clue.text: A fine romance, full of good humour

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades
a romance is a fanciful tale, a fable

explanation.surface: Describes a lovely love affair that is full of laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable is friendly and easy to talk to, cheerful in temper.

clue.text: Spare no established player

definitions.meaning: something spare is additional, surplus to need
a film ... is a walk-on performer, far from a star

explanation.definitionFit: A spare item is additional, and a bit-part film performer is called by the same word.

clue.text: Bloody child behind 80% of lawlessness!

indicators.note: the child's letters follow, coming behind, the shortened crime
four fifths of a five-letter word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: crime is lawlessness
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a youngster is behind most of the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: '80% of' takes four of the five letters of CRIME, leaving CRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is the deep red colour of blood, so bloody here is a colour word.

clue.text: What's said to be complete fleece

indicators.note: what is said is what is heard, so the word is matched by sound with another spelling

parts.note: sheer means complete, as in sheer nonsense

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether something counts as a complete swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' is a verb here: to cut a sheep's wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece a sheep is to cut off its wool, which is what shearing does.

clue.text: Wastrel filling barrel dithered around

indicators.note: around means the letters picked out are turned to read backwards
the letters sit inside the words like filling in a sandwich

explanation.surface: A layabout is stuffing a barrel and has been hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' picks RELDI from inside 'barrel dithered'; 'around' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a good-for-nothing who wastes time, a lazy loafer.

clue.text: Smallest rabbit ultimately getting most irritation?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the itchiest thing gives the most irritation

explanation.surface: A tiny rabbit ends up as the most irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCHY is informal British for tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is informal British for very small, so its superlative means the tiniest.

clue.text: Sesame to cultivate: large leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for large goes from the word

parts.note: to till land is to cultivate it
L is short for large on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Planting sesame, the big leaves appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the departure verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Til is an Indian name for the sesame plant and its oil-bearing seeds.

clue.text: Rope that's ritually burned?

definitions.meaning: a rope used to hold a tent or mast steady
the effigy of ... Fawkes burned on bonfires each 5 November in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: On Bonfire Night (5 November) Britons burn an effigy of Guy Fawkes, who tried to blow up Parliament in 1605.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent rope is a guy line, and the bonfire effigy of Fawkes is known by the same name.

clue.text: One leaves coaches, wild about inventor's latest conveyance

indicators.note: one figure leaves, departing from the word and so dropped from it

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wild word goes around the letter

parts.note: a feral animal is wild

indicators.note: latest means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A passenger quits the coaches, wild about an inventor's newest vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' suggests vehicles to match 'conveyance' but it is the verb, train. 'Leaves' takes I out; 'about' wraps the wild word round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A transferral is the act of moving something from one place to another, a conveyance.
